---
title: "Week 1 Exercises - First Steps in the Shell"
---

Short, **ungraded** practice tasks for this week - about 20-30 minutes total. Nothing is turned in; the goal is simply to get your hands on the keyboard before next class. Bring any snags to class or office hours. Companion reading: [Ch. 4](../book/chapters/04-unix-fundamentals.html) and [Ch. 6](../book/chapters/06-computer-systems.html); keep [App. A](../book/chapters/appendix-A-shortcuts.html) and [App. B](../book/chapters/appendix-B-unix.html) open as you work.

1.  Open **Positron** and open the integrated terminal (**Ctrl-\`**). Run `echo $SHELL` - which shell are you running?
2.  Run the toolkit check: `R --version`, `python3 --version`, and `quarto --version`. Write down the three version numbers (you will need them when asking for help).
3.  Run `pwd`. What is the absolute path of your home directory?
4.  Create a home for your course work: `mkdir -p ~/projects/comptools`, then `cd` into it and confirm with `pwd`.
5.  Go back to your home directory and run `ls -a`. Find one *hidden* file (its name starts with a dot). What is it?
6.  Run `man ls` and find out what the `-t` option does. Quit the manual with `q`.
7.  Using **Tab completion only**, `cd` into `~/projects/comptools` typing as few characters as you can.
8.  Press `↑` to re-run your `pwd` command, then try `Ctrl+R` and type `mkdir` to search your command history.
9.  Run `sleep 30`, notice the prompt does not return, and cancel it with `Ctrl+C`.
10. Find your laptop's specs (macOS: Apple menu → About This Mac; Windows: Settings → System → About): how many CPU cores and how much RAM? Compare with one standard Talapas node (128 cores, 512 GB).
